text:
devon: evening handoff — noticed an EU-side cache drift affecting KV prefetch hit ratios since ~16:30 UTC. Not an outage but increased token latency for some short requests, and a couple noisy alerts fired for >2x baseline miss_rate. putting it on the overnight watchlist :wave:

marta: thanks — do you have a short checklist for us to follow if it spikes? any safe mitigations we can flip from oncall? :eyes:

devon: short checklist: 1) check `kv.prefetch.miss_rate` and `kv.latency.p50` on grafana (EU stack). 2) if miss_rate >3x baseline for >5m, enable temporary prefix-caching fallback (route prefills to larger cache tier). 3) if encoder latency rises, reduce prefetch window to limit KV pressure. 4) escalate to infra if we see >30% CPU with persistent miss_rate.

Quick commands:
```
# query recent miss rate (last 15m)
curl -s "http://grafana/api/ds/query" -d '{query: "kv.prefetch.miss_rate{region=\"eu\"}[15m]"}'
# silence noisy alert rule (one-off)
amtool silence --start=now --end=2h "rule=kv_prefetch_noise_eu"
```

kevin: FYI the alert is pretty sensitive to short bursts. i'd rather tune the rule than silence long-term. i'm going to open a tiny PR to shift evaluation window from `1m` -> `5m` for the EU rule unless someone objects.

sam: +1 on tuning rule. oncall, if you hit the silence command make sure to add a comment with reproduction links. also leave the prefills fallback instructions in the channel so rotation knows what to do.

devon: updated runbook snippet pasted to Confluence: https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/kv-prefetch-eu — shortlink in the ticket. i'll be reachable until 19:30 UTC then switching off; tagging coverage for overnight.

oncall-bot: reminder: coverage swap scheduled at 20:00 UTC. @marta -> oncall until 08:00 UTC. Reaction requested :bell:

marta: got it, i'll take the rotation. i'll watch miss_rate and encoder p50 for the first hour. if anything crosses thresholds i'll follow the checklist and ping oncall. thanks devon.

kevin: opened PR #4021 to extend evaluation window and added a note about metric aliasing causing false positives. please review when you have a moment.

sam: leaving a quick note — if you see metric aliasing, try toggling `metrics.namespace_alias` in debug view to confirm (cheap check).

devon: perfect. adding a link to the PR in the runbook and leaving a couple of dashboard panels pinned. good handoff. :thumbsup:
